name: Myotonic Dystrophy

prevalence.range: DM1: 1 in 3,000 to 1 in 8,000 depending on population

ethnicAssociations: DM1 affects all ethnicities; most common muscular dystrophy in adults of European descent
DM1 extremely high prevalence in Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean region of Quebec (founder effect)
DM2 primarily affects populations of European descent
DM2 very rare in other ethnicities

criteria.description: Clinical myotonia (delayed relaxation after muscle contraction)
Progressive distal weakness and wasting (DM1) or proximal weakness (DM2)
CTG repeat expansion in DMPK gene (DM1) or CCTG repeat expansion in CNBP/ZNF9 gene (DM2)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation with CTG repeat expansion in DMPK (DM1) or CCTG expansion in CNBP (DM2). Clinical features support testing but genetic test is definitive.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: DM1 CTG repeats: normal 5-34, premutation 35-49, pathogenic 50-~4000+. DM1 shows anticipation with maternal transmission causing congenital form. DM2 does not have congenital form and is generally milder. Congenital DM1 presents with hypotonia and respiratory failure in neonates.

pathognomonic.notes: Inability to relax muscles after contraction; handshake difficulty; 'warm-up' phenomenon
Hand grip weakness, foot drop; characteristic distal pattern (DM1); DM2 is proximal
Temporalis and masseter wasting, ptosis, long thin face, frontal balding (hatchet face in DM1)

common.notes: Christmas tree or multicolored cataracts on slit lamp; can appear before other symptoms
First-degree AV block, bundle branch block, atrial flutter/fibrillation; sudden cardiac death risk
Central hypersomnolence, not just from respiratory failure
In both males and females; DM1
From pharyngeal muscle weakness and myotonia

occasional.notes: Executive dysfunction, reduced initiative; more prominent in DM1

rare.notes: Only in DM1; neonatal hypotonia, respiratory failure, feeding difficulty; intellectual disability
Multiple calcifying epitheliomas; associated with DM1

laboratory: Fasting glucose and HbA1c for diabetes screening
imaging: MRI brain: white matter lesions, temporal lobe atrophy (DM1)
Slit lamp examination: posterior subcapsular iridescent cataracts
genetic: DM1: CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion in DMPK gene (chromosome 19q13.3); normal <34, pathogenic 50-4000+
DM2: CCTG tetranucleotide repeat expansion in CNBP/ZNF9 gene (chromosome 3q21.3); normal <26, pathogenic 75-11000+
Congenital form almost exclusively maternally transmitted (DM1)
DM2 does not show significant anticipation or congenital form
other: EMG: myotonic discharges (waxing and waning motor unit 'dive bomber' sound)
ECG: PR prolongation, QRS widening, atrial arrhythmias
Holter monitoring and electrophysiology study for cardiac evaluation
Sleep study for central and obstructive sleep apnea

distinguishingFeatures: MG has fatigable weakness, not myotonia
MG has ptosis that worsens with sustained upgaze
MG has normal EMG (no myotonic discharges)
MG has positive AChR or MuSK antibodies
IBM affects older adults with finger flexor weakness
IBM has characteristic muscle biopsy findings
Myotonia congenita has myotonia without dystrophy (progressive weakness)
Myotonia congenita does not have systemic features
Myotonia congenita has mutations in CLCN1 (chloride channel)

redFlags: Sudden cardiac death from arrhythmias is a major risk; annual ECG and periodic Holter monitoring mandatory
Anesthetic risk: exaggerated sensitivity to sedatives, opioids, and neuromuscular blocking agents
Respiratory failure may develop insidiously; monitor FVC regularly
Congenital DM1 in neonates: floppy infant with respiratory failure; mother may be undiagnosed
Pregnancy complications: preterm labor, polyhydramnios, postpartum hemorrhage
Cognitive and behavioral features may be underrecognized and impact adherence
references: Johnson NE, et al. Evidence-based management of myotonic dystrophy type 1. Neurology. 2021;96(2):e1-e14.
Meola G, Cardani R. Myotonic dystrophies: an update on clinical aspects, genetic, pathology, and molecular pathomechanisms. Biochim Biophys Acta. 2015;1852(4):594-606.
Turner C, Hilton-Jones D. Myotonic dystrophy: diagnosis, management and new therapies. Curr Opin Neurol. 2014;27(5):599-606.
